ideas.title: Duel Flip
ideas.pitch: A 2-player-first push-your-luck card game where both players flip into one shared, visible river.

comparables.name: Flip 7
comparables.difference: Makes 2P the primary mode, uses shared information and cuts random take-that.

comparables.name: Sea Salt & Paper
comparables.difference: Faster and push-your-luck rather than drafting.

comparables.name: Skull / Cacti-style bluffers
comparables.difference: No hidden bluffing; skill is in risk management.

ideas.evidence: Push-your-luck card games are at peak demand (Flip 7 is described as the most popular game of the past year). Flip 7 reviewers dislike its lack of a dedicated 2-player mode and its heavy luck. Gap evidence is thin: BGG and some pages could not be opened.
sources: Gamefound case study (Invincible: The Card Game)
ideas.notes: Pitched early as a feasibility test after one revision (critic: REVISE-MINOR). Seeded from games/duelflip/brief.md.

ideas.title: Solo/co-op micro deck-builder
ideas.pitch: A very small deck-building game that works solo and co-operatively.
ideas.evidence: Scored 22/30 as candidate B in Duel Flip's brief. The brief records only the name and scores, so player count, length and evidence were not kept. 2026-10-03 scan: solo play is a top-3 component of 2020-2025 releases, which supports demand.
ideas.notes: Seeded from the candidates table in games/duelflip/brief.md. Details are null because the brief did not record them.

ideas.title: 4-6 player party trick-taker
ideas.pitch: A party-sized trick-taking card game for four to six players.
ideas.evidence: Scored 20/30 as candidate C in Duel Flip's brief. The brief records only the name and scores.
ideas.notes: Seeded from the candidates table in games/duelflip/brief.md. Gap scored low (2), so research it more before choosing it.

ideas.title: Three-Hand Trick-Taker
ideas.pitch: A trick-taking game built around exactly three players, where each seat has a different role (leader, chaser, spoiler) that rotates each round.

comparables.name: The Crew
comparables.difference: Competitive, not co-op, and tuned for 3 rather than scaling 2-5.

comparables.name: Skull King
comparables.difference: No bidding; rotating roles instead of chaotic scoring.

comparables.name: Hearts (3-player variant)
comparables.difference: Needs card removal house rules; this is designed for 3 from the start.

ideas.evidence: Search summaries confirm 3 is the awkward player count for card games (destructoid and others). Trick-taking is hot (LOTR: Fellowship about 12,900 plays; Gamefound trick-taking bundle funded). Brief check: The Crew is BGG 7.8 but best at 4; Fox in the Forest (7.1) is 2-player only.
ideas.notes: Strongest gap evidence in this scan. Check seat balance carefully in simulation. Brief written 2026-10-03 from scan 2026-10-03.

ideas.title: Silent Duo
ideas.pitch: A 2-3 player co-op deduction card game where players may only communicate by the card they play, solving a hidden number sequence together.

comparables.name: Bomb Busters
comparables.difference: Fewer components, no talking at all, ends in 20 minutes.

comparables.name: The Crew
comparables.difference: Deduction of a shared sequence, not trick-taking.

comparables.name: Sky Team
comparables.difference: Cards only, no dice or board.

ideas.evidence: Bomb Busters had about 13,900 plays by March 2026 and a BGG geek rating of 7.4 (about 7,750 ratings); co-op articles stress games that avoid the quarterback problem through restricted talk (hexagamers 2026 co-op list, Sky Team recommended).
ideas.notes: Bot simulation needs a communication model; simulatability reduced to 4. Brief written 2026-10-03 from scan 2026-10-03.

ideas.title: Pocket Tableau
ideas.pitch: A 1-4 player engine-building tableau game in a tuckbox where each turn activates one row of double-sided cards.

comparables.name: Wingspan Pocket
comparables.difference: Original theme and a solo scoring ladder; no licence tie.

comparables.name: Sea Salt & Paper
comparables.difference: Engine rather than set collection.

ideas.evidence: Wingspan Pocket (July 2026, 1-5p, 25-35 min) shows a big publisher moving into this exact format, so demand is proven but the gap is closing. Solo is top-3 component for recent releases.
ideas.notes: Originality risk: needs a distinctive twist beyond 'Wingspan lite'.

ideas.title: All-at-Once Draft
ideas.pitch: A 2-5 player microgame where everyone secretly picks and reveals at the same time, so there is no waiting and rounds last two minutes.

comparables.name: Sushi Go
comparables.difference: No passing hands; a shared market is contested by simultaneous reveals.

comparables.name: 7 Wonders
comparables.difference: Far shorter and lighter.

ideas.evidence: Downtime is the most repeated complaint in review search results (Wyrmspan, Oath); simultaneous games like Sushi Go are named as the fix (gnomestew).
ideas.notes: Crowded corner; needs a strong twist on the reveal mechanic.

ideas.title: Tug of Crowns
ideas.pitch: A 2-player card duel on a single tug-of-war track where each side has a different 20-card deck with its own rules.

comparables.name: Twilight Struggle (card engine)
comparables.difference: 15 minutes, 40 cards total, no board.

comparables.name: Star Realms
comparables.difference: No deck-building; fixed asymmetric decks.

comparables.name: Jaipur
comparables.difference: Direct interaction on a shared track, asymmetric sides.

ideas.evidence: Two-player focus is an identified trend (search summary of 2026 trends); under-two-hour games draw the strongest reactions. Asymmetry raises originality but makes balance the main risk (KPI: seat gap 5 points or less).
ideas.notes: Differs from Duel Flip: no shared river, no push-your-luck. Brief written 2026-10-03 from scan 2026-10-03.

ideas.title: Nine Fields
ideas.pitch: A 2-4 player area-control game played on a 3x3 grid of cards that flip and shift as players place pawns, in a 20-minute game.

comparables.name: Love Letter
comparables.difference: Spatial control rather than hidden hand elimination.

comparables.name: Onitama
comparables.difference: Area scoring, more than two players.

comparables.name: Res Arcana
comparables.difference: Much lighter; board is the cards.

ideas.evidence: Modular-map designs are noted among emerging mechanics in the hot-list search summary. Evidence is thin and unverified because BGG could not be opened.
ideas.notes: Low-evidence demand; judge it on the originality of the shifting grid.

ideas.title: Pocket Village Pad
ideas.pitch: A cosy roll-or-flip-and-write for 1-4 players using a tear-off pad, where you build a village by drawing a few connected shapes each turn.

comparables.name: Cozy Stickerville
comparables.difference: Pencil only, no stickers; cheaper to print.

comparables.name: Welcome To...
comparables.difference: Shorter and spatial, with a solo score ladder.

ideas.evidence: Cosy and solo trends are both rising: Cozy Stickerville was named a top 2026 pick in one list; solo play is a top-3 component of 2020-2025 releases.
ideas.notes: Roll-and-write is crowded; the twist must be in the drawing rule.

ideas.title: Eight Nights
ideas.pitch: A 1-3 player co-op deck campaign in one tuckbox, played over eight 20-minute sessions with a few sealed envelopes of changes.

comparables.name: Aeon's End
comparables.difference: Much smaller, with fixed sealed content.

comparables.name: Pandemic Legacy
comparables.difference: Eight short sessions rather than a year-long campaign.

ideas.evidence: Solo and short-session trends support it, but the sealed envelopes make bot testing and prototyping harder. No direct sales evidence found.
ideas.notes: Borderline. Campaign state is hard to simulate; prefer other ideas.

ideas.title: Hedgehog Hurry
ideas.pitch: A 2-5 player co-op race for ages 6+ where the table plays cards to move a shared pawn home before a timer deck runs out.

comparables.name: Hoot Owl Hoot!
comparables.difference: Adds light hand-management for older kids and parents.

comparables.name: Forbidden Island
comparables.difference: 15 minutes, 40 cards.

ideas.evidence: Flip 7 reached ages 8+ and 2 million sales, showing family-friendly small-box appeal; no kids-specific evidence was found in this scan.
ideas.notes: Evidence weakest of the batch; verify demand before choosing.

ideas.title: Collectible duel card game
ideas.pitch: A trading card game with booster packs.

comparables.name: Cyberpunk TCG
comparables.difference: n/a

ideas.evidence: Cyberpunk TCG raised over $13M but with a licensed IP and a professional studio. A solo creator cannot print, balance or distribute boosters.
ideas.notes: Rejected: needs a licence, a large print run and hundreds of cards to balance. Not suited to a solo prototyper.

ideas.title: Fifty-Two Workshop
ideas.pitch: A 1-4 player engine-builder played with nothing but a standard 52-card deck plus a printed rule card, where suits are resources and ranks are upgrade levels.

comparables.name: Wingspan Pocket
comparables.difference: Needs no custom cards at all; a printed rule sheet is the entire product, so setup is seconds.

comparables.name: Sprawlopolis
comparables.difference: Engine building with a standard deck, not a custom 18-card puzzle.

ideas.evidence: Setup time is named as board gaming's top barrier to getting games played, and small-box, solo-capable games are the rising format. Standard-deck engine builders are scarce next to the many standard-deck solitaire and shedding games. Source pages opened: none (search summaries only).
ideas.notes: Originality vs nearest comparable: engine building is usually bound to custom card powers; here the powers come from the structure of a familiar deck (suit, rank, pairs), which no mainstream engine game does. Risk: balancing rank math; must feel like a game, not a solitaire variant.

ideas.title: Last Bid Standing
ideas.pitch: A 5-6 player auction card game where everyone bids at once with hidden coin cards and every losing bid is burned, so the table never waits.

comparables.name: Sushi Go
comparables.difference: Bidding with a burn-on-loss cost rather than drafting, built for 5-6 first.

comparables.name: Modern Art / For Sale
comparables.difference: Fully simultaneous, so no active auctioneer and no downtime.

ideas.evidence: Search summaries show few games are built for 5-6 players (most stop at 5) and a podcast episode in June 2026 praised six players as a sweet spot; downtime is a top complaint. Pages not opened (blocked or summaries only).
ideas.notes: Originality vs nearest comparable: auction games rely on turn-based escalation; here the burn-on-loss rule makes every bid a permanent cost, which changes the risk calculation. Moderate originality; needs a distinct scoring hook.

ideas.title: Three Against Three
ideas.pitch: A 6-player team card game where each side of three shares one secret signal vocabulary of card plays and must out-signal the other team within a 20-minute match.

comparables.name: Codenames
comparables.difference: Signalling happens through card play, not clue words.

comparables.name: Bridge-style partnership games
comparables.difference: Teams of three, no bidding system to learn.

ideas.evidence: Six players is described as an underserved sweet spot (podcast episode June 2026; lists note few games above 5). Team limited-communication games are praised as quarterback-proof in co-op articles. Evidence is thin; no sales data.
ideas.notes: Originality vs nearest comparable: 3v3 teams where signals are made by playing legal cards (a hidden channel inside the trick-taking), which Codenames and partnership games do not use. Hard to bot-test the signalling; simulatability 3.

ideas.title: Spy and Warden
ideas.pitch: A 2-player deduction duel where one player is secretly the spy and the other the warden, and each deduces the other's hidden goal from a shared pool of evidence cards in 10 minutes.

comparables.name: Love Letter
comparables.difference: Roles differ and goals are hidden both ways, not elimination by rank.

comparables.name: Hive Mind-style duels (generic)
comparables.difference: Pure deduction with no board.

ideas.evidence: The 2026 trend summary cites a return of social deduction and two-player focus as a rising area, but hidden-role games mostly need 5 or more players, so a true 2-player hidden-role game is rarer. Pages not opened.
ideas.notes: Originality vs nearest comparable: Love Letter hides a card; this hides a goal for both seats, so each player must both conceal and read. Moderate originality; verify balance across both roles.

ideas.title: Nine Lives Dungeon
ideas.pitch: A 1-player roguelike played with nine cards in a tuckbox, where each run rearranges the same nine cards into a new dungeon and a death changes the next run.

comparables.name: Friday
comparables.difference: Nine cards only, with a persistent lives track across runs.

comparables.name: One Deck Dungeon
comparables.difference: Ten minutes and no dice.

ideas.evidence: Solo reviewers rate small solo card games highly (Friday 4.5, Onirim 4.5 on Reddit-based summaries); solo is a top-3 component of recent releases; Opinionated Gamers highlight small portable boxes. Pages blocked.
ideas.notes: Originality vs nearest comparable: Friday and One Deck Dungeon grow or deplete a deck; here the nine cards are never added to, only rearranged and flipped, so the whole game is a permutation puzzle. Crowded solo space; the twist must carry it.

ideas.title: Row Walker
ideas.pitch: A 1-4 player card-path game where everyone lays cards into one growing path and a shared traveller token activates each card it reaches, so players fight over where the token goes next.

comparables.name: Everdell Journeys
comparables.difference: One shared token and one shared path instead of a path per player.

comparables.name: Wingspan Pocket
comparables.difference: Shared board state, so there is real interaction.

ideas.evidence: Everdell Journeys (card-path drafting, 1-6p, 30-60 min) reached about $446k from 3,593 backers against a $35k goal in September 2026, showing strong demand for card-path tableaus. That also means the format is being taken by an established brand.
ideas.notes: Originality vs nearest comparable: Everdell Journeys gives each player a personal path; a single shared token on a shared path makes it a contested-route game. Gap is low because a major publisher is in this space.

ideas.title: Ladder Pairs
ideas.pitch: A 4-player partnership climbing and shedding card game in which partners are chosen by a secret card each round, and the first team to empty both hands scores.

comparables.name: Tichu
comparables.difference: Partnerships are re-chosen each round and hidden, and the rules are shorter.

comparables.name: The Crew
comparables.difference: Competitive, shedding not trick-taking.

ideas.evidence: Trick-taking and card-play games with partners are strong in 2026 (The Crew, LOTR Fellowship, Gamefound trick-taking trio); climbing games are comparatively unrepresented in recent releases. Pages not opened.
ideas.notes: Originality vs nearest comparable: Tichu fixes partners at the table; hidden per-round partners turn it into a read-the-table game. Risk: partner reveal timing in bot play.

ideas.title: Last Ferry
ideas.pitch: A 5-6 player 15-minute hidden-traitor card game where nobody is ever eliminated, and the traitor must hide a quiet sabotage while the crew moves cargo card by card.

comparables.name: Werewolf-style games
comparables.difference: No elimination and no narrator.

comparables.name: Battlestar Galactica (traitor)
comparables.difference: 15 minutes and 30 cards.

ideas.evidence: Search summaries list the return of social deduction and gambling as a major 2026 trend, with traitor-in-a-co-op designs named. Complaints about elimination are common for the genre. Pages blocked.
ideas.notes: Originality vs nearest comparable: traitor games usually reveal through accusation; here the traitor is scored on stealth over time, so detection is gradual. Bots cannot model bluffing well, so simulatability is 3. Likely lower value for a bot-first pipeline.

ideas.title: Dead Reckoning
ideas.pitch: A 2-player card duel on a 5x5 grid of face-down cards where each player secretly plans a three-step path on paper and both paths are resolved together.

comparables.name: Onitama
comparables.difference: Moves are planned in secret and resolved at once, not alternated.

comparables.name: Battleship
comparables.difference: Shared uncertain terrain with movement, not guessing.

ideas.evidence: Two-player focus is an identified 2026 trend, and downtime is the top complaint; simultaneous planning removes waiting. Search results show a wide 2-player card game catalogue but no hidden-movement grid game. Pages blocked.
ideas.notes: Originality vs nearest comparable: Onitama alternates deterministic moves; simultaneous secret three-step plans create a rock-paper-scissors layer on a board. Overlaps in the grid idea with Nine Fields, so choose only one of them first.

ideas.title: Lantern Garden
ideas.pitch: A cosy 1-4 player co-op tuckbox where the table together plants and tends a shared garden of cards before a calm, non-violent weather deck ends the season.

comparables.name: Cozy Stickerville
comparables.difference: Co-operative, card based and reusable, not sticker consumables.

comparables.name: Forbidden Island
comparables.difference: No threat of losing; calmer weather-driven pressure.

ideas.evidence: Cosy games are a stated 2026 trend (Cozy Stickerville top pick, low rules threshold); co-op and solo both rising. No evidence of a gap for card-based cosy co-op specifically.
ideas.notes: Originality vs nearest comparable: low; the main difference is the calm failure-light co-op frame. Needs a real twist before use. Overlaps in audience with Pocket Village Pad.

ideas.title: Cartographer's Memory
ideas.pitch: A 1-5 player memory-and-draw game where cards show a hidden map briefly, then everyone draws what they remember, and scoring rewards the most plausible route rather than perfect copies.

comparables.name: Cartographers
comparables.difference: Pure recall and drawing; no polyomino placing or seasons.

comparables.name: Memoarrr!
comparables.difference: Drawing from memory, with plausibility scoring.

ideas.evidence: Simultaneous, low-downtime and cosy/solo-friendly formats are rising; memory games are rarely served in the hobby space. Evidence is thin, from trend summaries, with no direct sales data.
ideas.notes: Originality vs nearest comparable: scoring by plausible route (rules-checked against the map) rather than exact match is new; but pencil-and-recall is hard to bot-simulate, so rely on a proxy model.

ideas.title: Haggle Duel
ideas.pitch: A 2-player open-negotiation card game where players must trade goods using fixed exchange rates printed on a shared card row, and every trade must leave both sides better off in some way.

comparables.name: Jaipur
comparables.difference: Direct bilateral trades with a mutual-benefit rule, rather than market selling.

comparables.name: Catan (trading phase)
comparables.difference: Negotiation is the whole game, in 15 minutes for 2.

ideas.evidence: Search summaries show 2-player trading games are few and mostly market or selling designs, while two-player focus is rising. No direct evidence beyond catalogue listings; pages blocked.
ideas.notes: Originality vs nearest comparable: open negotiation almost always needs 3+ players; a mutual-benefit rule makes it work for two. Bots need a negotiation model; simulatability 3.

ideas.title: Big-box miniatures dungeon crawler
ideas.pitch: A campaign dungeon crawler with plastic miniatures and many scenarios.

comparables.name: Gloomhaven
comparables.difference: n/a

ideas.evidence: Crowdfunding giants fund miniatures-heavy projects, but long play times, setup time and table space are the recurring 2026 complaints, and a solo prototyper cannot produce plastic or hundreds of cards.
ideas.notes: Rejected: saturated, long setup, and miniatures cannot be prototyped cheaply by a solo creator.
